absent: Numeric values of policy constants, priority bounds, flag bits, error codes, and bandwidth shift constants.
Full layouts of task descriptor, run queue, root domain, deadline entity, and bandwidth structures.
Behavior of cpuset allowance query, mask restriction, mask application, and user mask bookkeeping.
Semantics of run queue pinning, double run queue locking, PI locking, and preemption guards.
Details of queued task transfer, wake preemption, stop execution on two processors, and remote reschedule.
Validation of deadline parameters, user permission checks, security hooks, and clamp handling.
Computation of normal and effective priorities, parameter installation, and class transition requeueing.
Lifecycle of balance callbacks and actions performed by deferred balancing.
Extensible scheduler enablement, switching, and teardown beyond the eligibility predicate.
Inactive timer operation, zero lag deferral, running bandwidth accounting, and server entity handling.

findings.text: Compatibility affinity management exposes operations to force an override mask derived from hierarchy information and to relax back toward the user requested mask. Forcing uses a temporary mask and applies the result with warnings on failure, while relaxing delegates restoration to the central affinity setter.

Affinity mutation is centralized in a routine that intersects the requested mask with cpuset allowance, validates deadline tasks, attempts the update, then rechecks for concurrent cpuset changes and may retry with a corrected mask while reporting invalidity. A separate check rejects deadline affinity changes that do not cover the whole root domain span when bandwidth control is active, with exemptions for non deadline tasks and special entities.

Task exchange between two processors validates distinct processors and mutual mask eligibility without locks, emits a NUMA swap trace event, then executes the exchange under a two processor stop routine. A remote preemption helper requests rescheduling on another processor when the target is currently running elsewhere under disabled preemption.

Scheduling policy mutation is exposed through a no check wrapper, a legacy parameter adapter that translates priority and nice plus reset on fork handling and custom slice propagation, and a main attribute based routine that performs validation, permission checks, bandwidth admission, class selection, and requeueing.

Per processor stop thread installation presents a FIFO like priority to user space, assigns the stop scheduling class, isolates its PI lock class for lock dependency tracking, and demotes any prior stop thread to the realtime class so it can terminate.

Balance callback handling provides extraction of the pending list from a run queue and later execution of that list under appropriate protection, allowing scheduling attribute changes to defer load balancing work until after lock release and PI adjustment.

Scheduling class choice maps deadline priority to deadline class, realtime priority to realtime class, and otherwise consults extensible scheduler eligibility before defaulting to fair class. Extensible scheduler eligibility accounts for global enablement, wholesale switching mode, teardown state, and policy identity, with enablement state read atomically.

Deadline admission control exposes overflow evaluation that computes new bandwidth from period and runtime, consults per root domain accounting, and updates totals for entry, parameter change, or exit cases. Ratio conversion, total adjustments, overflow predicate, capacity queries, and per run queue utilization updates support that decision.

Deadline identity is determined solely by equality of the policy value with the deadline constant, both for raw policy integers and for task descriptors via their policy field. Bandwidth enforcement is considered active exactly when the realtime runtime control is non negative. Special deadline entities are recognized by a governor flag only when frequency governor support is compiled in, otherwise never special.
The effective user affinity is the stored user pointer when present, otherwise the system wide possible mask. Relaxation of compatibility affinity uses this effective mask with no additional flags.

Bandwidth ratio treats infinite runtime as one full unit, zero period as zero to avoid faults, and otherwise scales runtime by a fixed shift divided by period. Overflow is reported only when a finite limit is configured and scaled limit is less than current total minus old plus new bandwidth.

Deadline capacity uses a fast path of active processor count shifted by capacity shift when asymmetric capacity handling is idle and the queried processor has default capacity, otherwise it sums per processor scaled capacities over the intersection of domain span and active set. Processor count for bandwidth likewise counts that intersection.

Compatibility forcing holds the hotplug read lock across mask restriction and final application so that concurrent offlining cannot cause silent migration failure. Temporary mask storage is released after unlock.

Queued task movement pins both source and destination run queue locks while transferring ownership and requesting preemption. The stop phase additionally holds both tasks PI locks together with both run queue locks before revalidating processor activity, current placement, and mutual mask eligibility.

Policy mutation acquires cpuset lock when either old or new policy is deadline, then the task run queue lock with clock update, and holds them across validation, class selection, and parameter installation. Balance callbacks are spliced under protection, the run queue is released with preemption disabled, PI is adjusted after cpuset release, then callbacks run under run queue lock with interrupts saved.

Total bandwidth mutation is serialized by the domain bandwidth lock, while per run queue extra bandwidth propagation and per run queue active bandwidth updates require run queue protection with scheduler RCU held. Capacity and membership queries assert scheduler RCU is held.

The swap argument aggregates two task references and two processor identifiers pairing each task with its expected current processor, allowing the stop routine to verify placement before exchanging destinations.

Affinity setting proceeds through allocation, cpuset intersection, deadline validation, initial commit, then re reads cpuset allowance. If the committed mask is no longer contained, it resets to current allowance, further intersects with prior user mask when user mode is indicated unless that would empty the set, recommits, and reports invalidity to signal the race.

Policy setting starts with parameter and permission validation, then enters a recheck loop that snapshots policy under run queue lock and restarts if a concurrent change is observed. When nothing changes except reset on fork it stores that flag and exits, otherwise it checks group and bandwidth admission, overflow, priority mapping with boost handling, class change marking, and deferred requeue with head versus tail choice based on priority direction.

Migration swap has an optimistic lockless filter for distinct active processors and mutual eligibility, followed by a stopped phase that rechecks activity, placement, and eligibility under full locks and fails with retryable status on any mismatch, otherwise moves queued tasks or records a wake target for sleeping tasks.

Overflow handling distinguishes entry of a non deadline task when no overflow would occur with adjustment for an armed inactive timer, parameter change of an existing deadline task with utilization propagation, and exit from deadline which defers total reduction to a later zero lag handler. Governor flagged tasks bypass accounting and unchanged bandwidth short circuits.

Run queue utilization change first clears non contending state, subtracts running bandwidth, attempts to cancel the inactivity timer and drops a task reference when cancellation succeeds for non server entities, then replaces old bandwidth with new in the run queue totals. Queued tasks skip propagation at the higher layer.

Primary mutation entries are the attribute based scheduler setter for policy and parameter changes, the affinity setter for mask changes, and the two task swap helper for NUMA movement. Supporting entries include compatibility force and relax helpers, stop thread installer, remote kick, and deadline overflow predicate used during admission.

Hazards include silent migration failure if hotplug protection is omitted, stale affinity after racing cpuset updates, admission of deadline tasks on partial domain spans, overflow of per run queue bandwidth totals, changing policy of the stop thread, PI induced balancing recursion via stop wakeups, run queue lifetime across unlock, and deadlock between wholesale extensible scheduler switching and teardown when new tasks route incorrectly.

Scheduling policy identifiers distinguish deadline, first in first out realtime, and extensible classes, with priority bounds separating deadline, realtime, and fair levels. Classification relies on these identities for class selection and validation.

Attribute flags control governor special status, reset on fork propagation, utilization clamp updates, and parameter preservation. A mask of all valid flags plus legacy reset bit translation defines accepted combinations, with governor requests rejected from user space.

Dequeue options preserve state across movement without clock update and mark class transitions, while enqueue direction selects head insertion on priority demotion from user view. Affinity control marks validation checks and user initiated updates with an optional saved user mask.

Negative error results signal invalid argument, busy admission conflict, out of memory, permission denial, and retryable stop failure. Bandwidth accounting uses an infinite runtime sentinel, a unit constant for full capacity, and shift constants for ratio and capacity scaling.
